acceptance.given: Q2 authoring is complete, and the Q2 change set and fixture changes are available for scope validation.

oracle.expected: A scope check of the Q2 changed paths passes only when every changed path is within the four declared test modules, scripts/sc/tests/skill_quality_support.py, or scripts/sc/tests/fixtures/skill-quality/**, and fixture changes are limited to positive, boundary, negative, legacy, or migrated fixtures.
forbidden: Any Q2 change is outside the declared test/helper/fixture allowlist.
Any Q2 change modifies a production file or the requirements input.
Fixture changes fall outside the five permitted fixture classes.
oracle.observable: The scope-check result identifies the inspected changed paths and fixture classes, and reports whether the exact allowlist constraints pass.

acceptance.then: The scope check passes only if the changed paths and fixture classes satisfy the exact Q2 allowlist.
acceptance.when: During Q2 scope validation, inspect the changed-path set and fixture changes; evaluate the scope-check result as a structural boundary check.

failure_intents.selector_intent: The Q2 scope check must fail when the changed-path set contains a path outside the frozen test/helper/fixture allowlist, includes a production or requirements-input change, or includes a fixture outside the five allowed classes.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Author Q2 test, helper, and fixture content only within the frozen allowlist, and verify the resulting changed-path and fixture-class boundary.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No runtime state or schema changes; revert any compiler scope-check change while preserving frozen requirement inputs.

slice_hint.state_transition: Q2 authoring changes are restricted to the four declared test modules, the test support helper, and the skill-quality fixture subtree; production and requirements inputs remain unchanged.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The Q2 scope check passes with every changed path inside the exact test/helper/fixture allowlist and every fixture change classified as positive, boundary, negative, legacy, or migrated; it fails for any out-of-scope path or fixture class.
